correctness.rationale: The real Lipschitz-free vertex space with the graph shortest-path metric is the weighted ℓ1 edge-flow quotient by the cycle space. Disjoint cactus cycles split this as an ℓ1 direct sum, each cycle quotient being ℓ1(C,w)/span(1_C), plus bridge coordinates. The basis from a spanning tree omits exactly one edge a_C from each cycle. Since an operator norm on such a quotient is the maximum of its values on unit edge generators, signed tree-edge diagonal operators have unit ratios on retained geodesic edges; the omitted-edge image gives min_t[h|t|+Σw_e|ε_e+t|], attained at t=−1,0,1. This equals min(S,h+S−|S_+−S_-|) and maximization over signs gives the exact discrepancy K=max(1,max_C min(S_C,h_C+S_C−Δ_C)/h_C). Weighted geodesicity enforces edge endpoint distances w_e, including all boundary cases. For integer lengths, K_C=S_C/h_C iff Δ_C≤h_C. The reduction from even-total PARTITION maps retained lengths to 2a_i and omitted h=1, preserves simple-cycle geodesicity and uses parity to force Δ∈{0}∪[4,∞), proving NP-completeness for binary encoding. Independent exact dual-section vertex maximization matches the formula on six separately selected weighted/unweighted cycles.
